messages:
ben (customer): hey team, hitting a weird spike of 429s + retries this morning after a clock sync on our infra. python sdk 0.14.2. retries look correlated — many clients retry at the same moment and we see brief thundering, then a wave of 503s from the edge.

marie (support): thanks — can you paste minimal repro + env? is this gunicorn/uvicorn, container, k8s? also do you set any SDK env vars for jitter/seed?

ben (customer): repro is simple, running under gunicorn with preload_app off actually, but we recently rolled an OS update that ran ntp sync at ~03:10 UTC. snippet: 
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['RW_KEY'])
for _ in range(200):
    try:
        client.generate(prompt='x' * 32)
    except Exception as e:
        print('ERR', e)
```
we're not setting any jitter env vars. logs show repeated calls with identical X-Idempotency-Key headers at the same second.

marie (support): curious — 0.14.2 changed jitter seeding behavior last patch, pinging @aj from SDK team.

aj (sdk-eng): looking. we switched to seeding our jitter rng on module import with int(time.time()) in v0.14.0 to get deterministic dev behavior, but that can collide after clock adjustments. if multiple processes import at very nearby times they can end up with the same seed.

srijan (runtime): also possible: if processes are forked after import (preload_app=true) the RNG state is duplicated across children leading to correlated jitter. but ben said you had preload_app off, so less likely. can you confirm gunicorn flag?

ben (customer): we have preload_app=false but we saw the ntp drift by ~120s — a bunch of containers synced at once. the SDK prints an rng seed in DEBUG logs: "jitter_seed=1701234567" repeated across many hosts.

aj (sdk-eng): that matches. two failure modes: 1) seeding from wall-clock -> simultaneous seeds when clocks align; 2) reseed-on-every-request path that accidentally used a coarse timestamp leading to repeated seeds within same second. either yields near-zero entropy leading to synchronized jitter values.

marie (support): can you paste the debug log excerpt where idempotency header repeats? also which http client adapter (requests, aiohttp)?

ben (customer): here's trimmed log: 
```
[2026-03-02T03:10:12.102Z] client: generate -> idempotency_key=ab12cd... jitter_seed=1701234567 sleep_ms=0.000
[2026-03-02T03:10:12.103Z] client: generate -> idempotency_key=ab12cd... jitter_seed=1701234567 sleep_ms=0.000
[2026-03-02T03:10:12.103Z] upstream: 429 Too Many Requests
[2026-03-02T03:10:12.203Z] client: retry -> idempotency_key=ab12cd... jitter_seed=1701234567 sleep_ms=0.000
```
we use requests v2.31 and running in k8s with cron node OS updates.

aj (sdk-eng): thanks — that log shows RNG produced identical jitter for each call (sleep_ms=0). that's the bug. root cause: rng seeded with int(time.time()) and then in the backoff path we erroneously do quick reseed using same timestamp if current time - last_seed < 5s, which in some code paths became a no-op but left deterministic state.

marie (support): short term mitigation for you: set env RW_BACKOFF_JITTER_SEED to a high-entropy value (e.g., container start random from /dev/urandom) or upgrade to 0.14.3 we just cut that forces use of os.urandom for seed and avoids reseed-on-each-call.

ben (customer): can confirm setting RW_BACKOFF_JITTER_SEED prevented the spike in our staging. will schedule upgrade to 0.14.3. any guidance on idempotency header duplicates? we saw same key repeated.

aj (sdk-eng): idempotency key duplication is secondary: our default idempotency key generator used call-site timestamp + small counter; if jitter is identical and code path does immediate retry with no sleep, you'll see same key reused across retries in same process. fix in 0.14.3: stronger idempotency key using uuid4 + monotonic nanoseconds.

srijan (runtime): one more note — if your orchestrator does bulk restart/ntp at once, many clients across machines can align. Recommend staggered node reboots or use k8s disruptionBudget + randomized startup delay.

ben (customer): thanks. what's the expected behavior for 429/503 handling after upgrade? we want graceful backoff and no repeated identical idempotency keys.

aj (sdk-eng): post-0.14.3 behavior: jitter seeded from os.urandom per process at import; no reseed per request; idempotency keys incorporate uuid4 and monotonic_ns so retries look unique even across synchronized clients; default backoff uses randomized base jitter so aggregated retries spread. also added a debug flag RW_BACKOFF_VERBOSE for internal tracing.

marie (support): I'll open a support ticket for this customer and mark as resolved once they confirm upgrade. ben, ping here after you cut the upgrade and run the quick repro.

ben (customer): will do — thanks everyone. saved our weekend. :pray:

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: sdk/0.14.3 -> canary -> infra (2026-03-02T09:12:01Z) :rocket:
